newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Astra reports modest profit gain.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Astra reports modest profit gain.

text.p: Sweden's largest company Astra AB on Monday posted a slight lift in profits for the first nine months of 1996.
Astra reported an eight precent rise in pre-tax profit to 9.85 billion Swedish crowns ($1.5 billion) in the period to Sept. 30 against market expectations of 9.81 billion crowns.
"It was a good, solid report with no great surprises," analyst James McKean of Morgan Stanley said.
Sales rose 2 percent in Astra's key European markets and 19 percent in North America, giving an overall rise of 5 percent to 28.14 billion crowns ($4.27 billion).

Astra said the stronger crown made comparisons with 1995 less flattering. After hedging, the stronger crown wiped 600 million crowns ($91 million) off results in the first six months of the year and another 150 million ($23 million) in the third quarter.
The crown was expected to have negative impact of another 150 million crowns ($23 million) in the fourth quarter.

Astra cited higher sales for its leading drug, the antipeptic ulcer agent Losec. This included sales in the United States, where Astra markets Losec in conjunction with Merck & Co. Inc through joint venture vehicle Astra Merck.
Sales of Astra's second largest drug, the anti-asthma agent Pulmicort, edged up 3 percent.
